clue.text: First signs: mound under mandible, perhaps, swelling?

definitions.text: First signs: mound under mandible, perhaps, swelling?

indicators.note: the opening letters, or first signs, of the five words that follow are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A doctor lists the early symptoms of an illness: a lump under the jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First signs' takes the initials of mound, under, mandible, perhaps, swelling; the whole clue also describes the disease's early symptom.
explanation.definitionFit: The infection is known for a painful swelling of the salivary glands just below the jaw.

clue.text: Principal party takes on second steward

parts.note: major means chief or principal
a do is a party
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: The main party appoints a deputy as head servant.
explanation.definitionFit: The head servant of a large household runs it as chief steward.

clue.text: Parrot with head of myna and a cry of a rook

indicators.note: only the leading letter of the bird's name is taken

parts.note: caw is the call of a rook or crow

explanation.surface: A bird chorus: a myna and a rook calling.
explanation.definitionFit: This large brightly coloured bird is a type of tropical American parrot.

clue.text: Splendid, for example, to have nothing on one's conscience

parts.note: super means splendid
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: It's splendid to have a clear conscience with nothing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Freud's theory this part of the mind acts as the conscience.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian psychology this is the part of the psyche acting as moral monitor.

clue.text: Bandy-ball encouraged

parts.note: in bowls or cricket a bowl is a ball delivered
egged on means encouraged

explanation.surface: A sports report: a game of bandy, with the ball spurred onward.
explanation.walkthrough: Bandy looks like the hockey-like game, with ball part of the same picture, but it is the adjective meaning bent outward at the knees.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandy legs curve outwards, which is exactly what this hyphenated adjective describes.

clue.text: Batsman's first boundary? Yes, well over!

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the cricket word is taken

parts.note: a rim is an edge or boundary

explanation.surface: A cricket crowd cheers the batsman's first boundary going clear over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boundary' looks like a four or six in cricket but is an edge; to fill to the top and spill is to run over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that brims spills over the edge, the top of a well full and running over.

clue.text: Degree of brilliance on face of an old timer

parts.note: the water of a diamond is its lustre and grade, as in of the first water
clock is slang for a person's face

explanation.surface: The shine on an elderly person's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old timer' looks like a veteran but is an ancient device; 'on' places one piece before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Before mechanical clocks, a vessel dripping water measured time, a timepiece of antiquity.

clue.text: Fly or flea, would you say?

definitions.meaning: to fly is to run away
spoken, flea is the same as flee, to run away

explanation.surface: Asking whether an insect is a fly or a flea.
explanation.definitionFit: To get away is to fly or flee, and flea sounds like flee.

clue.text: Sad, losing out with sliding-scale

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy account of losing out on a wage scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges the letters of SAD and LOSING; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this is a rapid slide through a run of notes, a scale played sliding.

clue.text: Stag, perhaps, embracing female is put off

indicators.note: the animal's name wraps round the other letter, as in an embrace

parts.note: a stag is an example of a deer

explanation.surface: A stag cuddles a doe and is repelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone something is to delay it until later.

clue.text: Means to raise subject of the merry man, in a word

parts.note: a jack is a device for lifting a car or other weight
a point is a topic or matter under discussion

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on lifting gear and the topic of a jolly fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Point is the jester in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Yeomen of the Guard, whose song is 'I have a song to sing, O' about the merry man and his maid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gilbert and Sullivan jester sings of the merry man in The Yeomen of the Guard.

clue.text: Kind of hanger that produces a scar?

definitions.text: Kind of hanger that produces a scar?

parts.words: Kind of hanger that produces a scar?
parts.note: the word goes before hanger to make a tense serial ending, and a scar is a steep rocky face, which it is

explanation.surface: A coat hanger that leaves a mark on the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scar' suggests a wound, but in northern English a scar is a steep rock face; the word also completes 'hanger' as a suspense ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheer rock face is a scar in dialect, and a suspenseful serial ending is a kind of hanger named after it.

clue.text: Deserts bloody conflict in the interior

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other, placed in its interior

parts.note: bloody describes something red
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a gory war in the heart of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserts' looks like a verb (abandons) but is the noun, as in just deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: One's just deserts are what one has earned, a recompense for one's conduct.

clue.text: He is the first to speak on behalf of a Pretender

definitions.text: He is the first to speak

parts.note: pro means for, on behalf of
a poser is one who pretends or puts on an act

explanation.surface: A herald speaks up first for a claimant to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: In a formal debate the mover of the motion speaks first. 'Pretender' suggests a claimant like the Old Pretender, but here is a show-off.
explanation.definitionFit: In a formal debate, the person moving the motion opens the speeches.

clue.text: Ornament to bring home?

definitions.meaning: to decorate a book with pictures
to make a point clear, drive it home

explanation.surface: Decorating a house to take home.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate a text with pictures, or to make a point clear with examples.

clue.text: Dutch house-white — a bloomer,' regionally distributed!

parts.note: the House of Orange is the Dutch royal family
lily-white means pure white

explanation.surface: A Dutch royal house, all pure white, makes a blunder spread across regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder but means a flower. 'Regionally distributed' is the setter's flourish: the flower grows wild in parts of Europe and is the emblem of Ulster's Orangemen.
explanation.definitionFit: This lily is a flowering plant, and any flowering plant is a bloomer.

clue.text: Prints like water-colours

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water, used as a prefix meaning watery
tints are colours or shades

explanation.surface: Pictures painted in watercolour.
explanation.definitionFit: These are etchings made by a process that gives tonal effects like wash drawings.

clue.text: Workers in a building society?

parts.note: these birds are not bank clerks but members of a flock that builds one shared nest together

explanation.surface: Staff at a mortgage lender.
explanation.walkthrough: A building society is a British savings and mortgage institution; here it is read literally as a society that builds, a group of tropical cuckoos sharing a communal nest.
explanation.definitionFit: These American cuckoos live in groups and build one communal nest, a literal building society.

clue.text: One enters translation of Wyatt for example

indicators.note: a translation changes the form, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes up translating the poet Wyatt.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas Wyatt brought the sonnet form into English from Italian, translating Petrarch, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas Wyatt was a Tudor poet who wrote and translated many fourteen-line poems.

clue.text: Over Kidderminster, say, it is held in angle of flight

definitions.text: Over Kidderminster, say, it is held in angle of flight

parts.words: Over Kidderminster, say, it is held in angle of flight
parts.note: Kidderminster is a type of carpet; a metal bar lies over a staircase carpet in the angle of each step

explanation.surface: An aircraft's angle as it passes over a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kidderminster is an English town famous for carpets, so stands for a carpet; a flight is a staircase, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal bar fixed across the angle between tread and riser keeps the stair carpet in place.

clue.text: A burden to old seamen

parts.note: the NUS was the National Union of Seamen

explanation.surface: Retired sailors are a weight on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Union of Seamen, a British trade union, gives NUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a duty or responsibility that weighs on someone.

clue.text: May live with an old English character

parts.note: quick means living, as in the quick and the dead
thorn is the Old English letter for th

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone lives with an elderly Englishman of note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like a verb or month but is the hawthorn blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn, also called may, is the hedging shrub of this name.

clue.text: Fabulous spinner, reluctant to be held by county

indicators.note: one word is held inside the other abbreviation, which wraps it

parts.note: loth means reluctant

explanation.surface: A legendary storyteller who is unwilling to be detained by the county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means of fable or myth: she is the Fate who spins the thread of life.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the Fate who spins the thread of each life.

clue.text: The First of Foot find something useful for bootlessness

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: a utility is something of use

explanation.surface: A regiment, the First of Foot, finds a handy object for those without boots.
explanation.walkthrough: The First of Foot was a famous infantry regiment. 'Bootlessness' means pointlessness, not lacking boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootless is an old word for useless, so bootlessness is pointlessness.

clue.text: Destined, we hear, to be lionized

indicators.note: this marks a word that sounds like the answer when said

parts.note: fated means destined

explanation.surface: Someone fated to be celebrated, so the rumour goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To be celebrated and made much of is to be fêted or treated like a celebrity.

clue.text: Cycle enclosure

explanation.surface: A bicycle shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle is a round of events that comes back to its start; an enclosure can be a ring or round fence.

clue.text: Seat of Oxford companion to music?

definitions.text: Seat of Oxford companion to music?

parts.words: Seat of Oxford companion to music?
parts.note: a seat in the furniture sense, an Oxford professorship, and the furniture that goes with music in a party game

explanation.surface: A reference book about music, the Oxford Companion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oxford Companion to Music is a reference book; here a professor at Oxford holds a seat, and musical seats is the party game.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a piece of furniture to sit on, a university professorship, and in a party game it pairs with music.

clue.text: Detain a guy

definitions.meaning: a rope supporting a mast or tent

explanation.surface: Holding a man back.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt something is to hold it; a supporting rope on a ship's mast is also known by this name.

clue.text: Reversible conviction?

indicators.note: the answer reads the same backwards, so it can be turned round unchanged

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A court verdict that can be overturned on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversible conviction' looks like a quashable verdict; conviction is a belief, and the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or firmly held belief is a doctrine one is convinced of.

clue.text: Take it in turns to be deputy

definitions.meaning: to swap back and forth one after another

explanation.surface: Sharing the duty of standing in for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means swap back and forth; as a noun, a substitute who stands in.

clue.text: Scott's craft in exploration

definitions.meaning: the ship Captain Scott took to the Antarctic in 1901

explanation.surface: A polar explorer's vessel on an expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's Antarctic ship bore the name, and the noun also means finding new things.

clue.text: Painter and engraver of ruder pieces

indicators.note: the word ruder is broken into pieces and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An artist who made coarser works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' looks like artworks but is the signal to break up RUDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was the German Renaissance artist famed for woodcuts and copper engravings.
